title.narrative: Enhancing the protection of affected people, especially women and girls, including prevention and response to gender-based violence.

description.narrative: The drought situation has increased the vulnerability of adolescent girls, women, people with disability, as well as those with long-term health conditions such as HIV/AIDS and TB. With the likelihood of compromised' social support and safety systems, women and girls are at greater risk of malnutrition, transactional sex, teenage pregnancies, GBV and school drop-out. The CERF Protection Project will focus on the four identified districts that rank high in food insecurity: Quthing, Maseru, Mohale's Hoek, and Qacha's Nek. Five per cent of the population in each district is classified as Emergency (IPC Phase 4). The interventions implemented will protect the rights and dignity of the most vulnerable and guard the gains made in improving the protection of the vulnerable and ensuring access to SRHR service. The Project will implement the following; 1. Ensuring that the most vulnerable women and girls, including those living with disabilities, have their dignity restored and are protected from engaging in negative coping mechanisms, including sex for food. By providing a Six-month supply of dignity kits to the most vulnerable, their dignity will be restored, and the burden of securing necessities will be minimized, thus protecting them from engaging in negative coping mechanisms. The project will target 1250 women in each of the four districts.2. Rehabilitation and provision of safe shelter for women and girls who have experienced Gender-based violence. With the current conditions of safe spaces in the country, a much-needed rehabilitation of an alternative space will ensure that those who are experiencing GBV are taken to safe spaces and supported to improve their livelihoods and thus less vulnerable to further violence. The rehabilitation of the safe spaces will ensure that more women in need of shelter can be accommodated and provided with the necessary psychosocial support and necessities.3. Towards the project's implementation, UNFPA will ensure that "protection" principles are mainstreamed across all sectors, including in projects of other agencies. UNFPA will support the identification of protection threats related to the different activities and monitoring indicators to ensure the centrality of protection in all assistance provided. This will ensure interventions strictly adhere to the 'do no harm' approach. PSEA and SGBV initiatives will be strengthened to address identified risks linked with the impacts of the drought emergency. This will be achieved by integrating protection messaging into the implementation of the projects.4. The families and households that have been identified to receive support are often experiencing multifaceted challenges of vulnerability, including poverty, experience of violence and discrimination. The provision of psychosocial support services to vulnerable families that are receiving assistance to link them with other social protection services will be instrumental in addressing the unseen impact of the crisis. This activity will be implemented with the support of auxiliary social workers working in the identified communities. The provision of PSS also ensures that post the project phase, there is no dependency syndrome and that the beneficiaries are capacitated to improve their livelihoods.
